title: Embedded Team Hiring & Partnership Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview:

Purpose
- This playbook defines a standard hiring, onboarding, and partnership approach for candidates hired into embedded roles: engineers, product managers, designers, and data scientists who will be placed inside product or platform teams but remain connected to a central enabling org. The goal is to reduce ramp time, set predictable expectations for managers and candidates, and preserve consistent quality across decentralized placements.

Scope
- Applies to: Embedded hires (E-embedded) and long-term cross-functional contractors joining product, platform, and data teams.
- Exclusions: Purely central roles (e.g., hiring for people-ops core HR team) and short (<12 week) contractors.

Principles
1) Clarity of scope: hire against an initial 90-day charter with measurable deliverables.
2) Observable outcomes: bias toward work samples and past impact over hypotheticals.
3) Partnership-first: hiring loop must include both hiring manager and a partner (product, infra, design) as interviewers.
4) Inclusion: structured interviews, diverse slates, and calibrated scorecards mitigate bias.

Hiring workflow (high level)
1. Intake & role brief (owner: hiring manager + central recruiter)
   - One-pager: mission of placement, success metrics at 30/60/90 days, required/optional skills, team context, escalation contacts.
   - Candidate profile: seniority band, travel/region constraints, remote vs colocated requirement.
2. Sourcing & shortlisting
   - Minimum slate size: 4 diverse candidates before onloop interviews when possible.
3. Interview loop (see template below)
4. Decision & offer (people-ops approves comp band & equity)
5. Onboarding and 90-day sponsor assignment

Role intake template (deliverables to include in the brief)
- 30-day goals (examples): Setup dev environment, ship first small bugfix or doc change, join oncall shadowing.
- 60-day goals: Deliver initial feature component or experiment, own recurring weekly sync with partner team.
- 90-day goals: Independently land a scoped project with post-deploy metrics and a blameless retro.
- Ramp success metrics: PR merged within 2 weeks; first independent deploy by week 8; oncall readiness by week 12.

Interview loop template (embeds and roles)
- Recruiter screen (30m): logistics, motivation, culture fit
- Work-sample assignment or take-home (optional for senior roles)
- Technical competency (45–60m): hiring manager + team engineer (system design, code review of candidate sample)
- Cross-functional partnership (30–45m): product/design/infra partner checks collaboration and prioritization
- Behavioral & leadership (30m): people manager or senior IC for collaboration examples
- Bar-raiser / calibration interviewer (30m): someone neutral from another org to assess bias and comp

Scoring rubric (sample)
- Each interviewer uses a 1–5 scale with evidence notes. Aggregate pass threshold: mean >= 3.6 and no single interviewer with a 1.
- Competencies (scored separately): Core craft (technical/product/design), Collaboration & Stakeholder Management, Ownership & Impact, Learning Agility, Communication.

DEI guardrails (mandatory)
- Diverse slate policy: at least 30% underrepresented candidates in final 4 when possible.
- Structured question bank supplied to interviewers.
- Interviewer calibration every 2 months for hiring managers who have conducted >4 loops.

Offer & acceptance checklist
- People-ops: confirm comp band, manager: confirm 90-day charter and sponsor, Legal: confirm any contract clauses (NDA, export control).
- Candidate: receives written offer with clear first-day logistics and expected 30/60/90 deliverables.

Onboarding & first 90 days (detailed plan)
- Role sponsor: someone on the host team (peer-level) assigned for 90 days; sponsor runs weekly sync during first 8 weeks.
- First week (Day 1–5):
  - Day 1: Welcome, account access, security & compliance training, team intro readout slot.
  - Day 2–5: Environment setup, mini pairing sessions, first 1:1 with manager (set expectations), meet cross-functional partner.
- Weeks 2–4: Shadowing on-call, ship first small task, feedback checkpoint at week 4 with manager + sponsor.
- Weeks 5–8: Ownership of a scoped feature/experiment; biweekly demo to partner team.
- Weeks 9–12: Handover, production metrics, oncall readiness signoff, end-of-90-day retro and success rubric review.

90-day evaluation (manager + sponsor)
Table (text format)
| Dimension | Evidence | Expected by 90 days | Rating notes |
|-----------|----------|---------------------|--------------|
| Ramp speed | PRs, deploys, code reviews | PR merged within 2 weeks, independent deploy by week 8 | 1–5 |
| Impact | Metrics, feature outcomes | Clear measurable impact (adoption, latency, cost) | 1–5 |
| Collaboration | Meeting notes, stakeholder feedback | Regular partner syncs and positive peer feedback | 1–5 |
| Reliability | Oncall incidents handled, pager response | Participated in oncall rotations; minimal guidance by week 12 | 1–5 |

Manager responsibilities (checklist)
- Prepare the 90-day charter prior to offer acceptance.
- Schedule first-week meetings and assign a sponsor.
- Run weekly 30-minute check-ins for first 8 weeks, then biweekly 1:1s.
- Provide timely feedback: short-form written notes after major milestones (PRs, demos).
- Submit 90-day evaluation to people-ops and file calibration notes.

Manager 1:1 and feedback cadence (recommended)- Weekly 30m manager check-ins for weeks 1–8: focus on blockers, onboarding logistics, psychological safety.- Weekly sponsor syncs (15m) run by sponsor.- Biweekly team sync demos (30m) to align stakeholders.- Formal 30/60/90 feedback checkpoints (written notes) at days 30, 60, 90.

Performance calibration & promotions
- Calibration windows: quarterly (standard) + rolling promotion packet review for exceptional cases.
- Evidence required for promotion: consistent 6–12 month impact, demonstrated leadership in scope expansion, peer & partner endorsements.
- Promotion packet template: summary of impact, before/after metrics, two manager-level endorsements, learning plan for next level.

Probation & remediation
- Probation period: default 90 days with extension possible (max 60 days) when there is a documented improvement plan.
- Remediation steps: document concerns -> create 30/60 day improvement plan with SMART goals -> weekly progress checkpoints -> final assessment.

Operational checklists and templates (links)
- New hire 90-day charter template (copyable).
- Interviewer question bank (structured) and scorecard (spreadsheet).
- Sponsor handoff checklist.
- Sample offer language for embedded placements.

Sample new hire 30/60/90 charter (plain text)
- 30-day: Complete environment setup, write first microservice unit tests, attend three partner planning meetings.
- 60-day: Deliver first scoped experiment, increase test coverage by X%, drive one cross-team sync.
- 90-day: Ship project, monitor initial metrics for 2 weeks, prepare lessons-learned doc and present in retro.

Integrations with existing people-ops processes
- Use People-ops hiring portal to create requisition and track diverse slate compliance.
- Upload 90-day evaluation into the People-ops performance folder.
- Trigger learning resources (role-specific training playlists) automatically on hire.

Escalation & ownership
- Hiring disputes or offer escalations: escalate to Talent Lead (people-ops) -> Head of Recruiting -> CFO for comp exceptions.
- Onboarding blockers that prevent ramping: escalate to host team tech lead and People-ops onboarding coordinator.

Appendix: sample interview scorecard (text)
- Candidate name: ____________________
- Role: ____________________
- Interviewer: ____________________
- Date: ____________________
- Scores (1–5): Core craft: __, Collaboration: __, Ownership: __, Communication: __, Overall: __
- Evidence notes: (3–5 bullet lines)
